```{r}
#| label: obx-setup
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONSOLE FACSIMILES -- render scaffolding, hidden (include: false). Same
# mechanism as anova.qmd: pane_facsimile.R defines the capture-once /
# display-twice helpers in their own dot-named environment (.obx). Each block
# below is one call whose code STRING is both printed into the page and
# executed once, so the shown code and the run code cannot drift. An
# unexpected error in any block HALTS the render (the publish gate).
#
# Devices, by the OUTPUT-REGISTER rule: the prose READS the output of blocks
# 1, 2 and 4, so those panes render OPEN (.obx$show_console(fence = TRUE)).
# Block 3's output names the render machine's jstats folder, a real path the
# facsimile's leak check refuses (rightly), so block 3 is a plain fence and
# its output is QUOTED from a run at render in a text box, the working
# directory and the jstats folder replaced by placeholders the prose names
# (chunk "listing"; a real path left in it halts the render).
#
# Nothing on this page writes outside the working directory.
#
# YOUR OWN TABLE STYLES, PAGE 1 (S422 review; Publication tables page 5
# before it). Written as "Where your styles live",
# then split by Jeff (S422): this page makes the style folder and the copy;
# page 2, "Keeping your styles", has the .Rprofile line, the copies and the
# hidden jstats folder (the S421 draft's "Where to keep your styles").
#
# S428 (the S427 wording pass, Fable 5.2, okayed by Jeff): the topic's
# roadmap under the intro -- pages 3 to 5 are three ways to change a style,
# "pick one" (Jeff, S423: "keep the order and say pick one") -- and the
# page's numbered changes.
#
# jstats is NOT pre-loaded: block 1 teaches library(jstats), and R prints the
# startup message on first attach only. joutput()/joptions() are left alone. The
# page WRITES a styles folder and one style file into the working directory;
# the clean-slate lines below clear them before the blocks run, and the
# teardown clears them after. The styles folder goes only when left empty;
# the shared list below names every Publication tables page's files.
#
# HOW-TO LAYOUT (S344). No top boxes: the shared material lives once on
# howtos.qmd, and this page points there.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

options(width = 80)   # match a default 80-column console for table alignment
options(jstats.attach.noninteractive = TRUE)   # let block 1 show the real startup message

# THE SHARED LIST (S422): every Publication tables page's files, so a render
# halted on one page cannot leave a style file in the styles folder another
# page creates and lists. A styles folder still holding anything else HALTS
# the render: it is not this page's to remove.
.tables_files <- c("styles/myreport.jstyle", "styles/mystyle.jstyle",
                   "styles/myblue.jstyle", "styles/mytest.txt",
                   "styles/mytest.jstyle", "styles/mymatch.jstyle",
                   "myblue.txt", "mymatch.txt",
                   file.path("Tables", c("Descriptives.docx",
                     "Regression.docx", "Tables.docx", "Tables_v2.docx",
                     "Table1_mystyle.docx", "Table1_report.docx",
                     "Table1_myblue.docx", "Tables_mymatch.docx",
                     "Models.docx")))
.sf_clean <- function() {
  f <- .tables_files[file.exists(.tables_files)]
  if (length(f)) file.remove(f)
  if (dir.exists("styles") &&
      !length(list.files("styles", all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)))
    unlink("styles", recursive = TRUE)
  if (dir.exists("Tables") &&
      !length(list.files("Tables", all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)))
    unlink("Tables", recursive = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
.sf_clean()
if (dir.exists("styles"))
  stop("The project's styles folder holds files no Publication tables page ",
       "wrote. Move them out and render again.", call. = FALSE)

source("pane_facsimile.R")   # defines .obx (dot-named); turns the output color on
```

## Making your own style

**Your own table styles &middot; Page 1**\
*This topic builds on the Publication tables pages, which end with
[5. Choosing a style: apa or report](tables-choosing-a-style.qmd). Its pages are
numbered too.*

The two built-in styles, `apa` and `report`, can't themselves be changed. Your
own style starts as a copy of one of them, saved as a *style file*: a plain-text
file that lists every setting, each with a value you can change. This page is a
hands-on run-through of making that copy, in a folder of your own, and of how
jstats finds the copy by its name.

The rest of the topic goes on from that copy. Page 2 shows where to keep a
style you mean to keep. Pages 3 to 5 are three ways to change a style: by hand
(page 3), with an AI assistant (page 4), or with Posit Assistant (page 5). Pick
one. Page 6 matches the look of a published table, by page 4's route.

This page follows the pattern of every How-To: numbered blocks of code that
build one script, with the finished script to download at the bottom.
[Using the How-To pages](howtos.qmd#using-the-how-to-pages) explains the
pattern, and how to reset your session if something goes wrong.

### 1. Load jstats and the data

We'll work on `community`, one of the two practice datasets that ship with the
package: 103 simulated respondents to a community survey. `jload()` puts a copy
of it in your workspace, and `juse()` makes `community` the default data frame,
so the commands that follow can leave its name out.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 1. Load jstats and the data --------------------------------------

## Load jstats and the community practice dataset, and make community the
## default data frame. quiet = TRUE skips jload()'s report on what it
## loaded; overwrite = TRUE replaces a copy already loaded in this session
## without asking first
library(jstats)
jload("community", overwrite = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
juse(community))---", fence = TRUE,
  lead = "The command lines are shown; the standalone <code>##</code> comment lines aren't -- running a comment just echoes it back and does nothing.")
```

### 2. A style folder, and a copy in it

A *style folder* is the folder you choose for your style files.
`joptions(style.dir = )` sets it. On this page the style folder is a folder
named `styles` inside your project, and `jstyle()` with `save.as =` writes a
copy of `report` into that folder, under the name `myreport`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 2. A style folder, and a copy in it ------------------------------

## Keep this page's styles in a styles folder inside the project. jstats
## makes the folder; the setting lasts until R restarts
joptions(style.dir = "styles")

## Save a complete copy of report as myreport.jstyle in the style folder
jstyle("report", save.as = "myreport"))---", fence = TRUE)
```

`joptions()` confirms the style folder and, since there was no `styles` folder
yet, creates it. `jstyle()` then reports the copy it wrote, `myreport.jstyle`:
a style file's name ends in `.jstyle`.

### 3. Where jstats looks

`jstyle()` with nothing in the parentheses lists the styles jstats can find,
and the folders it looks in.

```r
## ---- 3. Where jstats looks --------------------------------------------

## The styles jstats can find, and the folders it looks in, in order
jstyle()
```

```{r}
#| label: listing
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Block 3, run here and QUOTED (see the setup chunk): the working directory
# shown as ~/your-working-directory, the jstats folder as <your jstats folder>.
# The listing reads a FRESH, EMPTY jstats folder, as a new reader's is: a
# temporary R_USER_DATA_DIR, which tools::R_user_dir() reads at each call. The
# render machine's own styles are its owner's, not the page's (S422: Jeff's
# render listed a style of his own, Testapa, from his jstats folder).
.sf_old_ud <- Sys.getenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = tempfile("sf-ud-"))
.sf_raw <- utils::capture.output(jstyle())   # all of it on standard output
.sf_jf  <- tools::R_user_dir("jstats")
if (is.na(.sf_old_ud)) Sys.unsetenv("R_USER_DATA_DIR") else
  Sys.setenv(R_USER_DATA_DIR = .sf_old_ud)
.sf_raw <- gsub("\033\\[[0-9;]*m", "", .sf_raw)  # a quotation: no color codes
.sf_sub <- function(x, path, to) {
  for (v in unique(c(gsub("\\\\", "/", path), path,
                     gsub("\\\\", "/", normalizePath(path, mustWork = FALSE)))))
    x <- gsub(v, to, x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}
.sf_txt <- .sf_sub(.sf_raw, .sf_jf, "<your jstats folder>")
.sf_txt <- .sf_sub(.sf_txt, getwd(), "~/your-working-directory")
while (length(.sf_txt) && !nzchar(trimws(.sf_txt[length(.sf_txt)])))
  .sf_txt <- .sf_txt[-length(.sf_txt)]
if (any(grepl("(?<![A-Za-z])[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]|/home/|/Users/|/root/|/tmp/", .sf_txt, perl = TRUE)))
  stop("listing: a real path survived the placeholders:\n", paste(.sf_txt, collapse = "\n"))
cat("```text\n", paste(.sf_txt, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

That is what the Console showed when this page was made. Where this page has
`~/your-working-directory` and `<your jstats folder>`, your Console shows the
full path of your own working directory and of your jstats folder.

When a call names a style, jstats looks for its file in three places, in this
order: the style folder, if one is set; your working directory (your project's
folder); and your *jstats folder*, a folder jstats keeps for you. It uses the first file of that name it finds,
so a style in the style folder wins over one of the same name anywhere else.
The two built-in styles are always there, and need no file.

### 4. A style found by its name

So `jtable()` can use `myreport` by its name alone, with no folder named.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 4. A style found by its name -------------------------------------

## Save a result, then make a table from it in myreport, which jstats
## finds in the style folder
d1 <- jdesc(Age, Income, WellbeingScore, print = FALSE)
t1 <- jtable(d1, style = "myreport"))---", fence = TRUE)
```

`jtable()` found `myreport` in the style folder and made the table in that
style. With no `file =`, `jtable()` writes no Word file, and says so.

`myreport` is still a copy of `report`, setting for setting. Page 2,
[Keeping your styles](tables-keeping-styles.qmd), shows where to keep a style
you mean to keep: the `styles` folder here is inside the project, and is
deleted when the project is. Pages 3 to 5 then show three ways to change a copy
like this one: pick one. Page 3, [Changing a style by hand](tables-by-hand.qmd),
is the first.

```{r}
#| label: prose-gates
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROSE GATES -- hidden. Each stopifnot() below is one statement the prose
# makes about what the package does; a false one HALTS the render, the same
# publish gate the blocks have. Each gate compares two runs that differ in the
# one thing the prose claims, so it can fail.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.msgs <- function(expr) {         # what a call prints, both streams, as one string
  m <- character(0)
  o <- withCallingHandlers(utils::capture.output(expr),
                           message = function(c) { m <<- c(m, conditionMessage(c))
                                                   invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  paste(c(o, m), collapse = "\n")
}
.lst <- paste(.sf_txt, collapse = "\n")
.sty <- local({                   # the names under "Styles", up to the blank line
  i <- which(.sf_txt == "Styles")[1]
  j <- which(!nzchar(trimws(.sf_txt)))
  j <- j[j > i][1]
  sub(" .*", "", trimws(.sf_txt[(i + 1L):(j - 1L)]))
})
.pos <- function(s) regexpr(s, .lst, fixed = TRUE)
# the search order: a myreport.jstyle in the working directory, set apart
# from the style folder's copy by its font, is read only when no style folder
# is set
.td <- tempfile("sf-"); dir.create(.td)
.wd_copy <- readLines("styles/myreport.jstyle", encoding = "UTF-8")
.wd_copy[which(.wd_copy == "font = Arial")[1]] <- "font = Courier New"
writeLines(.wd_copy, "myreport.jstyle", useBytes = TRUE)
.font_set   <- grep("^font ", utils::capture.output(jstyle("myreport")), value = TRUE)[1]
invisible(utils::capture.output(joptions(style.dir = NULL)))
.font_unset <- grep("^font ", utils::capture.output(jstyle("myreport")), value = TRUE)[1]
invisible(utils::capture.output(joptions(style.dir = "styles")))
file.remove("myreport.jstyle")
# joptions() creates a style folder that is not there: block 2's
.m_rel <- local({                 # block 2's call, in a fresh folder
  .old <- setwd(.td); on.exit(setwd(.old))
  .msgs(joptions(style.dir = "styles"))
})
.rel_made <- dir.exists(file.path(.td, "styles"))
invisible(utils::capture.output(joptions(style.dir = "styles")))
# block 4: found in the style folder; no file asked for
.m4 <- .msgs(jtable(d1, style = "myreport"))

stopifnot(
  # block 2: the copy written; a missing folder is created by joptions()
  file.exists("styles/myreport.jstyle"),
  grepl("Created 'styles' folder in working directory.", .m_rel, fixed = TRUE), .rel_made,
  # block 3: myreport listed, and only the styles a new reader has (none of
  # the render machine's own); the three folders, in order
  grepl("myreport", .lst, fixed = TRUE),
  identical(.sty, c("apa", "report", "myreport")),
  .pos("(the style folder)") > 0,
  .pos("(the working directory)") > .pos("(the style folder)"),
  .pos("(your jstats folder") > .pos("(the working directory)"),
  grepl("<your jstats folder>", .lst, fixed = TRUE), !grepl("\033", .lst, fixed = TRUE),
  # the first found wins: the style folder's copy, then the working directory's
  grepl("Arial$", .font_set), grepl("Courier New$", .font_unset),
  # block 4
  grepl("Table 1. Descriptive Statistics", .m4, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl("no Word file was asked for", .m4, fixed = TRUE)
)
unlink(.td, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Take the whole script with you

That's the full run-through. If you'd like the entire script in one file to
keep and reuse, download it here. Put your own style's name in place of
`myreport`, and, once you've set up a folder for every project, as page 2
shows, leave out the `joptions()` line.

The file is the finished version of the script you built: the same code, in the
same order. If you run the file again, `jstyle()` asks before replacing
`myreport.jstyle`; the file's first lines say what to answer.
[Using the How-To pages](howtos.qmd#using-the-how-to-pages) says more about
finished scripts and how to run one.
